steps.body: Put numbers in counting order from smallest to greatest: 2, then 5, then 8.
steps.narration: Put numbers in counting order from smallest to greatest: 2, then 5, then 8.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 11? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 11 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 12.
13 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 11 lands on 12.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 on from 11: you land on 12.
widget.successFeedback: 12 — one hop forward, and one hop later in the song always means greater.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 12.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 11 means one hop, stopping on 12.

cml.actionGoal: Pair the groups one to one, or place both numbers in the counting song, for kcm order numerals.
invariants: Comparison rests on two facts that never move: pairing one to one leaves the bigger group with leftovers, and a number later in the counting song always names more — which is what kcm order numerals uses.
misconceptions: Judging by how much space a group fills, by the size of the things in it, or by which number was written first.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more joined the smaller group, would the pairing come out even?

widget.prompt: Drag the numbers into counting order, smallest first.

misorderFeedback.feedback: 8 before 5 starts with the greatest value. Counting order begins with the smallest value, 5.
6 cannot come before 5 — the smaller number always stands earlier in counting order.

widget.missFeedback: Find the smallest value first, then place each next-greater number after it.

steps.body: A number line confirms the order: six comes before nine, so 6 is the smaller number.
steps.narration: A number line confirms the order: six comes before nine, so 6 is the smaller number.

widget.prompt: Start at 5 and make four one-steps. Use the landing to extend the ordered list.

commonLandings.feedback: That is the starting number. Complete all 4 hops.
That is one hop beyond 9. Stop after exactly 4 hops.

widget.successFeedback: 9 — the complete hop path lands on the requested greater number.
widget.lowFeedback: Check the start, direction, and number of hops before choosing the landing.

options.feedback: 16 is where we stood; the question asks for the next number along.
Correct — the later a number comes in the counting song, the greater it is, by one each step.
18 skips a number; the count moves one at a time.
15 comes BEFORE 16 and is the smaller neighbour, not the next one.

widget.prompt: Repair the mixed number cards by dragging them from least to greatest.

misorderFeedback.feedback: 10 before 7 starts with the greatest value. Counting order begins with the smallest value, 7.
8 cannot come before 7 — the smaller number always stands earlier in counting order.

widget.missFeedback: Find the smallest value first, then place each next-greater number after it.
widget.successFeedback: 7, 8, 9, 10 — the cards now run from least to greatest.

options.feedback: 6 is the smaller endpoint, not a number inside the pair.
8 is the larger endpoint; between means strictly inside.
Correct — 7 is greater than 6 and less than 8, sitting exactly between them.
9 lies beyond 8, outside the endpoints altogether.
